## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Restore the deleted defaults file before merge because `load_defaults()` still requires it. The port boundary, hidden configuration errors, and missing host-normalization coverage should also be fixed. This review read every changed file and the surrounding code and tests; no tests or other checks were run.

## Changes
The pull request adds millisecond timeout parsing, port validation, configuration loading, and host normalization with tests. It also deletes bundled defaults and adds reviewer documentation and a fixture.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore the defaults required by startup — Calling `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError` instead of returning `{"timeout":30}`. The unchanged reader at app/startup.py:6 still opens the deleted `defaults.json`. — Any caller loading the bundled defaults fails before receiving configuration.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 — For `is_valid_port(65535)`, you return `False` even though the documented range includes 65535. The strict upper comparison excludes this valid boundary value. — Callers reject a valid TCP port.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Preserve configuration failure details — Loading malformed JSON or a missing file returns `{}` because you catch every `Exception` without reporting it. Neither the docstring nor an adjacent comment explains the fallback or its caller-visible behavior. — Callers cannot distinguish a valid empty configuration from a read or parsing failure or identify the underlying cause.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Exercise trailing-dot removal — For `normalize_host("Example.COM.")`, the new trailing-dot branch has no test coverage. The only host-normalization test uses `"Example.COM"`, so removing the stripping logic would leave it passing. — Regression protection does not cover the promised removal of one trailing dot.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Align the documented empty-host return value — For `normalize_host("")`, you return `""`, contradicting the docstring’s “returns None when h is empty.” The empty-input branch explicitly uses `return ""`. — Callers relying on the documented `None` sentinel receive a different value.
